# Package management {#sec-appendix-package-management}

Reference material for managing packages, followed by background on R and its installation tools. For the basics, start with [Install & Update R Packages](install-update-r-packages.qmd).

## Introduction

This appendix covers package management beyond the basics. Packages are fundamental to R. More than 22,000 packages are available on [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/), the Comprehensive R Archive Network (as of September 2026; verify the current count at [cran.r-project.org/web/packages](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/)).

Packages are available for different [topics](https://cran.r-project.org/web/views/). You should always look for a package before writing code from scratch. If you have written your own code for a new analysis or topic, do share it with the R community by converting it into a package. You can learn more about building R packages from [R Packages](https://r-pkgs.org/), a book by [Hadley Wickham](https://hadley.nz/).

## Other package sources

### GitHub

Some developers make R packages available on [GitHub](https://github.com/) before releasing them on CRAN. We can install such packages using `install_github()` from the [devtools](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/devtools/index.html) or [remotes](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/remotes/index.html) package. You need to specify the name of the repository and the package. For example, we can download [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/) or [dplyr](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/) with this code:

```{r install2, eval=FALSE}
devtools::install_github("tidyverse/ggplot2")
remotes::install_github("tidyverse/dplyr")
```

### Bioconductor

[Bioconductor](https://www.bioconductor.org/) provides tools for analysis and comprehension of high throughput genomic data. Install the `BiocManager` package and use `BiocManager::install()`:

```{r install4, eval=FALSE}
# install BiocManager if needed
install.packages("BiocManager")

# install a Bioconductor package
BiocManager::install("GenomicFeatures")
```

> For faster installs with dependency resolution, you can also try `pak::pkg_install()` from the [pak](https://pak.r-lib.org/) package as a modern alternative.

## Install Different Versions

Now that we have learned how to install packages, let us look at installing different versions of the same package.

```{r install7, eval=FALSE}
remotes::install_version('dplyr', version = "0.5.0")
```

If you want to install the latest release from GitHub, append `@*release` to the repository name. For example, to install the latest release of dplyr:

```{r install8, eval=FALSE}
remotes::install_github('tidyverse/dplyr@*release')
```

## Installed Packages

- `installed.packages()`: view currently installed packages
- `autoload('function_name', 'package_name')`: load functions and data from packages only when called in the script
- `available.packages()`: packages available for installation
- `old.packages()`: packages which have new versions available
- `new.packages()`: packages not yet installed
- `remove.packages('package_name')`: remove installed packages

## Library Paths

A library is a directory that contains installed packages. Your system will usually have more than one R library. You can locate the libraries using `.libPaths()`.

```{r install9}
.libPaths()
```

Use `lib` to install or remove packages in a particular library, and `lib.loc` to load or update them.

### Install

```{r install10, eval=FALSE}
install.packages('stringr', lib = .libPaths()[1])
```

### Load

```{r install11, eval=FALSE}
library(lubridate, lib.loc = .libPaths()[1])
```

### Update Packages

```{r install12, eval=FALSE}
update.packages(lib.loc = .libPaths()[1])
```

### Remove Packages

```{r install13, eval=FALSE}
remove.packages('stringr', lib = .libPaths()[1])
```

> Explore Rsquared Academy's own R packages and guides at [pkgs.rsquaredacademy.com](https://pkgs.rsquaredacademy.com/).

## R background and installation tools

The rest of this appendix gives background on the organizations behind R and the tools used to install it.

## Organizations

### R Foundation

The R Foundation is a not-for-profit organization founded by members of the
R core team. It is responsible for the continued development of R. It also
supports the annual useR conferences. You can learn more about the R Foundation
[here](https://www.r-project.org/foundation/).

### R Consortium

The R Consortium supports the R Foundation and other key organizations
and groups developing, maintaining and using R. It funds projects that improve
the infrastructure around R and supports conferences and user groups
around the world. You can learn more about the R Consortium [here](https://www.r-consortium.org/).


## Installation

R is available for Windows, Mac and is part of many Linux distributions. You 
can download and install R from any of the CRAN mirrors listed [here](https://cran.r-project.org/mirrors.html).

### CRAN

[CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/mirrors.html) stands for **C**omprehensive **R**
**A**rchive **N**etwork. You can download R and user contributed packages
from here for different operating systems. CRAN is pronounced as KRAN or C-RAN.


### Extensions

User contributed packages can be downloaded from

- [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/mirrors.html)
- [Bioconductor](https://bioconductor.org/)
- [GitHub](https://github.com/topics/r?l=r)
- [R-Forge](https://r-forge.r-project.org/)

### R GUI

R comes with a simple GUI with sufficient features for data analysis and 
visualization.

```{r gui, fig.align='center', echo=FALSE, fig.alt='Screenshot of the base R GUI window'}
knitr::include_graphics('img/rgui.png')
```
